html:
Maurice Bishop was the lawyer who led the New Jewel Movement to power in Grenada in a coup in March 1979, overthrowing Eric Gairy. He headed the People's Revolutionary Government until 1983.

His government built schools and clinics, ran literacy and farm programmes, and made close ties with Cuba, whose workers began a new airport. Elections were never held.

In October 1983 a rival faction under Bernard Coard put him under arrest. A crowd freed him, but soldiers recaptured him and shot him with several ministers at Fort Rupert. Days later the United States invaded. Many Grenadians still honour him, and the airport is named after him.
